title: Peptide Vial Flag Labels vs Wraparound Labels: Is Extra Space Worth the Snag Risk?
seoTitle: Peptide Vial Flag vs Wraparound Label Guide
description: Compare a small research-vial wrap with an optional flag identifier. Learn where a flag adds legibility, where it catches in trays and what to test before quoting.
alt: AI-generated RP Research glass vials with full printed body labels, one carrying an additional two-sided identification flag
caption: AI-generated construction illustration, not a production or adhesive test. RP Research, PEPTIDE A and DEMO LOT 109 are fictional; the protruding flag needs testing in the buyer's real tray.
intro: A flag creates room for an identifier, but it also creates an edge that can catch in the pack.
sources: HERMA: Wrap-around labeling for small cylinders
Brady: Flag-label construction on small cylindrical items

title: Protein Powder Refill Pouch vs Tub Labels: Do Not Reuse the Tub Dieline
seoTitle: Protein Powder Refill Pouch vs Tub Label Guide
description: A flexible refill pouch and a rigid powder tub need different printable areas and application tests. Check zipper clearance, folds, label copy and SKU matching.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness cocoa protein powder tub and flexible refill pouch with different complete branded labels and dielines
caption: AI-generated packaging comparison. RP Wellness, DEMO 109, ingredient and nutrition-style text are fictional, not approved sale artwork or tested packaging.
intro: The refill pouch may share a brand identity with the tub; it should not inherit the tub's physical label file.
sources: HERMA: Labels for stand-up pouches and food packs
FDA: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide, general requirements

title: Clear vs Opaque Gummy Jar Labels: Show the Product Without Losing the Copy
seoTitle: Clear vs Opaque Gummy Supplement Jar Labels
description: Clear gummy-jar labels can reveal the product, but small print may disappear over colorful gummies. Compare clear film, white backing and opaque panels on the real jar.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness gummy jars comparing a transparent printed film label with white-backed copy against an opaque printed label
caption: AI-generated RP Wellness material concept. Gummies, DEMO LOT 109, icons and all product information are illustrative and are not approved supplement labeling.
intro: If the gummies become the background of every letter, the transparent effect can work against the buyer.
sources: Avery Dennison: Clear and white film label constructions
FDA: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide, general requirements

title: Hologram Seal on Shrink Film vs Carton: Which Surface Actually Opens?
seoTitle: Hologram Seal on Shrink Film vs Carton Guide
description: A hologram applied to outer shrink film behaves differently from one bonded to a carton flap. Decide what the seal should show, then test adhesion and opening evidence.
alt: AI-generated RP Secure hologram comparison on a film-wrapped carton and directly across a paperboard carton opening
caption: AI-generated placement comparison. RP Secure and DEMO 109 are fictional; the image does not demonstrate tamper performance or adhesive suitability.
intro: A sticker on disposable outer film cannot tell the same opening story as a sticker bonded across the carton joint.
sources: HERMA: Labels for logistics on shrink film and boxes
HERMA: Tamper-evident labels for film and paper packs

title: Hologram on a Warranty Card vs Carton Seal: Two Different Promises
seoTitle: Warranty Card Hologram vs Carton Seal Guide
description: A card hologram can mark a document, while a carton seal may show opening. Specify the proof, variable data and handling process for each without confusing their claims.
alt: AI-generated RP Secure hologram on a printed warranty card beside a separate holographic strip across a carton flap
caption: AI-generated RP Secure demonstration. Card, holograms and DEMO 109 are fictional; visual presence alone does not establish authenticity or tamper evidence.
intro: A hologram on a card says a card has a mark. It does not prove the package was never opened.
sources: HERMA: Product label with closure function
